problem:
Consider the equation in the variable $u,$ given by

$$
(q-5)u+9=0
$$

where $q$ is a constant. Given that this equation has no solution, what is the value of $q?$

$q=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
Suppose we have an equation of the form

$$
ax=b
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are constants, and $b\ne 0.$ If $a=0,$ then the equation has no solution.

First, let's write our equation in the form $au=b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(q-5)u+9 & =0 \\ (q-5)u+9-9 & =0-9 \\ {{(q-5)}_{⏟}}_{a}u & ={{-9}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation has no solution if

$$
q-5=0.
$$

Solving this for $q,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}q-5 & =0 \\ q & =5.\end{aligned}
$$
